title: Month 26
subtitle: The thirty-month visit is next month, and it is a short one.

baby.development: Your child says three words together, can jump with both feet off the floor, and can turn a page of a book. They are starting to sort by shape and color.

you.body: If you are pregnant again, the last trimester with a two-year-old is the hardest stretch. Ask for help with the lifting now.
you.mind: Twenty-six months is when the child starts to have a memory for what happened yesterday. That is what makes a routine comforting rather than just familiar.

coreActions.title: Book the thirty-month visit
coreActions.why: This is a short developmental check, and it is the visit where a language or movement concern is easiest to raise.
coreActions.detail: The thirty-month visit usually has no vaccines. The doctor will check language, movement, and teeth, and will ask about sleep and eating. Write down the sentences the child says so you can answer accurately.

coreActions.title: Practise jumping
coreActions.why: Jumping with both feet off the floor is a two-year-old milestone, and it is built by doing it.
coreActions.detail: Jump off a low step holding hands, then alone. Jump on a bed with you there. Jump over a line on the floor. A child who cannot jump by thirty months is worth mentioning at the visit.

coreActions.title: Keep the bedtime routine the same
coreActions.why: A predictable routine is what makes bedtime work at two, and it is easier to hold than to rebuild.
coreActions.detail: The same three or four steps in the same order, about twenty minutes, ending in the bed. Bath, teeth, two books, song, bed. A visual schedule on the wall helps a child who cannot read.

alsoKnow.title: Three words is on track
alsoKnow.body: Three-word sentences between twenty-four and thirty months are on track. A child who is not putting three words together by thirty months is worth raising at the visit.

alsoKnow.title: The full set of baby teeth is complete around three
alsoKnow.body: Twenty teeth, with the second molars last. A dental visit every six months from now is the usual schedule.

redFlags.text: Choking — cannot breathe, cough, or make a sound
A fever over 100.4°F with unusual sleepiness or a rash
Feeling hopeless, or thoughts of harming yourself or the child
